CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.finding: NOT REPAIRED, AND I STOPPED RATHER THAN CHANGING A SHARED MODULE. I independently reproduce VF26's number exactly: 27,981 dark pixels of the publishers' own printed ink are absent from the delivered pages, 802 on the bundle (201/200/201/200 on pages 1/3/7/9) and 27,179 on the inserts (10,372 on page 1, 12,656 on page 3, 4,151 on page 4). I also establish the CAUSE, which VF26 did not name and which is not where the earlier repair looked. Every one of the 33 /Ch dropdown fields across the two sources -- 66 widgets, 4 on the bundle and 62 on the inserts -- is shipped by the Coalition for Court Access with its /V ALREADY SET to a run of underscores that is one of that field's own /Opt entries. The publisher made the writing rule a selectable option and selected it as the published default; each widget's /AP /N draws exactly that rule (an opaque blank-state fill, a stroked baseline on 34 of the 62, and the underscores in the court's Times Roman) and nothing else. I checked every text-showing operand in all 66 streams: all 66 show only underscores. No prompt, no instruction to the filer, no substantive option word. scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-official-form-finalize.mjs then deletes them, at the block whose report key is `promptsSuppressed` (around line 1510): for every unwritten choice field whose selected value satisfies `isChooserPrompt`, it deletes /V AND deletes /AP from every widget. `isChooserPrompt` (scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-field-semantics.mjs:740) returns true for any value matching /^[\s_\-–—.·•]+$/ -- a pure run of underscores -- so a court's printed writing rule is classified as a chooser prompt and its appearance is destroyed. I ran the shared finalizer directly against each pinned source and it reports promptsSuppressed for all 32 insert dropdown fields and for the bundle's DD-cap-CourtType, by name.
CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.whyIStopped: The defect is genuinely in two shared modules and there is no lever at the caller, so my instructions say to say so and stop rather than change them. I did not stop on a guess: I BUILT the caller-side remedy the repository already provides for exactly this defect class, measured it, and reverted it. The appearance semantics registry (data/rcap-all50/shared/field-appearance-semantics.json, family-keyed, byte-neutral for every family without an entry) is the designed place to record that an appearance is the issuer's own, and Colorado JDF 417 already uses it for the same shape of defect -- a dropdown whose issuer-shipped /V is drawn by the form's own /AP and was dropped by the structural rule. I generated 4 family entries covering all 33 fields from the measured bytes (1,748 insertions, 0 deletions, no existing entry touched) and wired both builders to pass appearanceDispositions. IT MADE THE DELIVERED PAGE WORSE, and the measurement is why I reverted rather than shipped. Because `promptsSuppressed` has already deleted /AP before restrictWidgetContributions ever reads a disposition, preserving the field leaves pdf-lib with no appearance to preserve, so it SYNTHESIZES one from /MK /BC: I read the resulting flattened XObject out of the produced PDF and it strokes a full rectangle border and draws `<> Tj`, an empty string, in /Helvetica 11 -- a BOXED FIELD on a filing where the court prints a writing rule, and the court's own /BS /S /U says the border it declares is an UNDERLINE, not a box. Measured: insert page 1 went from added=2,450/removed=10,372 to added=16,134/removed=1,812, and I cropped and looked at the pixels rather than trusting the totals. Turning on suppressSynthesizedWidgetBorders instead only removes /MK /BC, which yields an appearance that paints nothing -- the same blank page by another route. There is no option among the finalizer's thirty that exempts a field from `promptsSuppressed`; the block is unconditional and is not reachable from appearanceDispositions, which is itself the structural defect: the finalizer has a documented caller-supplied mechanism for deciding what an appearance MEANS, and this block destroys the appearance before consulting it. Repairing it means either narrowing isChooserPrompt so a pure writing rule is not a prompt, or gating promptsSuppressed on the disposition registry. Both change bytes for the forty-odd families that share the finalizer, and that is not a repair lane's decision. I changed neither module. The working tree carries no part of the reverted experiment: I re-ran both builders afterwards and both reproduce the committed fixture digests exactly.

Both belong to in_section1_petition, whose waitingPeriods carry 'The arrest, charge or allegation, whichever is later' and 'Written agreement of the prosecuting attorney' / 'Early filing permitted', and whose generationRequirements carry a required key prosecutorWrittenAgreementEarlyFiling that this track does not have (I compared the two generationRequirements arrays: 10 keys against 11, that key the only difference). I wrote no rule the record does not state, and where it is silent I left it unsaid and said that it is silent. SERVICE.finding: The refusal was right on the bytes and is now disclosed. The build refuses participant.street_address on List-MailingAddresses_LEA, correctly -- the shared binder had been matching the participant's own home address onto a block whose printed label the census reads as the two control characters BEL and ACK, so the order a judge signs named the petitioner's home as a law-enforcement agency's service address. What failed was that nothing told the participant. Before this repair participant-instructions.md contained 0 occurrences of 'Law Enforcement Agencies', 0 of 'page 14', 0 of 'law enforcement' in any case, and no row in its supply table for any page above 8; step 8 told the participant the opposite, that the order's directions to the agencies 'are the court's' and to 'Check those and leave the rest'. After this repair the guide names the block 4 times, page 14 three times, and every one of the box names List-MailingAddresses_LEA, CountyClerkAddress, MailAddressSheriff, Prosecutor, ProsecutorMailingAddress, LEA1, LEA2 and LEA3. Step 8 is rewritten to distinguish the order's findings and decree, which are the court's, from its ADDRESS BLOCKS, which are not findings. A new section, 'The proposed order asks for addresses, and this packet supplies none of them', states the count and the reason for each block.
SERVICE.whatIRefusedToWrite: The committed record is SILENT on who completes the order's distribution list and the law-enforcement list. I checked: the track's rules.service says only 'The court serves the prosecuting attorney. The CCA appearance form nonetheless carries a certificate of service to the county prosecutor; follow the form', and a case-insensitive search of the whole track object returns 0 hits for 'distribution', 0 for 'sheriff', 0 for 'law enforcement', 0 for 'agenc' and 0 for 'clerk'. So the guide says the record does not state it, and sends the participant to the clerk. I invented no filing fee, no clerk's practice, no service rule and no deadline.

clonedFamilyPackets.whatIDidAboutIt: Nothing to the bytes, on purpose. My instructions say deciding this by adding a cosmetic variation would be worse than leaving it, and I agree on the evidence: the two tracks are two eligibility pathways over ONE published Coalition for Court Access bundle, and the publisher designed it that way -- the proposed order recites relief 'for an arrest, criminal charge, or juvenile delinquency allegation that did not result in a conviction', which covers both tracks in one sentence. Nothing in either track's registry entry names a field either document has and the other does not. The honest statement is therefore: THE TWO TRACKS GENUINELY PRODUCE THE SAME FILING AND DIFFER ONLY IN GUIDANCE, and after this repair they differ in guidance MORE than before, because the waiting-period paragraph is now generated from each track's own record instead of both carrying the section-1 rule.
clonedFamilyPackets.theOwnerQuestionIRaiseRatherThanAnswer: Should two packet families exist at all where one published bundle serves both tracks? No prompt, no instruction to the filer, no substantive option word. scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-official-form-finalize.mjs then deletes them, at the block whose report key is `promptsSuppressed` (around line 1510): for every unwritten choice field whose selected value satisfies `isChooserPrompt`, it deletes /V AND deletes /AP from every widget. `isChooserPrompt` (scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-field-semantics.mjs:740) returns true for any value matching /^[\s_\-–—.·•]+$/ -- a pure run of underscores -- so a court's printed writing rule is classified as a chooser prompt and its appearance is destroyed. I ran the shared finalizer directly against each pinned source and it reports promptsSuppressed for all 32 insert dropdown fields and for the bundle's DD-cap-CourtType, by name.
CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.whyIStopped: The defect is genuinely in two shared modules and there is no lever at the caller, so my instructions say to say so and stop rather than change them. I did not stop on a guess: I BUILT the caller-side remedy the repository already provides for exactly this defect class, measured it, and reverted it. The appearance semantics registry (data/rcap-all50/shared/field-appearance-semantics.json, family-keyed, byte-neutral for every family without an entry) is the designed place to record that an appearance is the issuer's own, and Colorado JDF 417 already uses it for the same shape of defect -- a dropdown whose issuer-shipped /V is drawn by the form's own /AP and was dropped by the structural rule. I generated 4 family entries covering all 33 fields from the measured bytes (1,748 insertions, 0 deletions, no existing entry touched) and wired both builders to pass appearanceDispositions. IT MADE THE DELIVERED PAGE WORSE, and the measurement is why I reverted rather than shipped. Because `promptsSuppressed` has already deleted /AP before restrictWidgetContributions ever reads a disposition, preserving the field leaves pdf-lib with no appearance to preserve, so it SYNTHESIZES one from /MK /BC: I read the resulting flattened XObject out of the produced PDF and it strokes a full rectangle border and draws `<> Tj`, an empty string, in /Helvetica 11 -- a BOXED FIELD on a filing where the court prints a writing rule, and the court's own /BS /S /U says the border it declares is an UNDERLINE, not a box. Measured: insert page 1 went from added=2,450/removed=10,372 to added=16,134/removed=1,812, and I cropped and looked at the pixels rather than trusting the totals. Turning on suppressSynthesizedWidgetBorders instead only removes /MK /BC, which yields an appearance that paints nothing -- the same blank page by another route. There is no option among the finalizer's thirty that exempts a field from `promptsSuppressed`; the block is unconditional and is not reachable from appearanceDispositions, which is itself the structural defect: the finalizer has a documented caller-supplied mechanism for deciding what an appearance MEANS, and this block destroys the appearance before consulting it. Repairing it means either narrowing isChooserPrompt so a pure writing rule is not a prompt, or gating promptsSuppressed on the disposition registry. Both change bytes for the forty-odd families that share the finalizer, and that is not a repair lane's decision. I changed neither module. The working tree carries no part of the reverted experiment: I re-ran both builders afterwards and both reproduce the committed fixture digests exactly.

SERVICE.finding: The refusal was right on the bytes and is now disclosed. The build refuses participant.street_address on List-MailingAddresses_LEA, correctly -- the shared binder had been matching the participant's own home address onto a block whose printed label the census reads as the two control characters BEL and ACK, so the order a judge signs named the petitioner's home as a law-enforcement agency's service address. What failed was that nothing told the participant. Before this repair participant-instructions.md contained 0 occurrences of 'Law Enforcement Agencies', 0 of 'page 14', 0 of 'law enforcement' in any case, and no row in its supply table for any page above 8; step 8 told the participant the opposite, that the order's directions to the agencies 'are the court's' and to 'Check those and leave the rest'. After this repair the guide names the block 4 times, page 14 three times, and every one of the box names List-MailingAddresses_LEA, CountyClerkAddress, MailAddressSheriff, Prosecutor, ProsecutorMailingAddress, LEA1, LEA2 and LEA3. Step 8 is rewritten to distinguish the order's findings and decree, which are the court's, from its ADDRESS BLOCKS, which are not findings. A new section, 'The proposed order asks for addresses, and this packet supplies none of them', states the count and the reason for each block.
SERVICE.whatIRefusedToWrite: The committed record is SILENT on who completes the order's distribution list and the law-enforcement list. I checked: the track's rules.service says only 'The court serves the prosecuting attorney. The CCA appearance form nonetheless carries a certificate of service to the county prosecutor; follow the form', and a case-insensitive search of the whole track object returns 0 hits for 'distribution', 0 for 'sheriff', 0 for 'law enforcement', 0 for 'agenc' and 0 for 'clerk'. So the guide says the record does not state it, and sends the participant to the clerk. I invented no filing fee, no clerk's practice, no service rule and no deadline.

clonedFamilyPackets.whatTheOneByteIs: Font size in a flattened appearance, over an identical value in an identical rectangle. The arrest builder opts into `fitTextPerWidget`; the section-1 builder instead sorts each field's widgets narrowest-first before handing the census to the finalizer. clonedFamilyPackets.whatIDidAboutIt: Nothing to the bytes, on purpose. My instructions say deciding this by adding a cosmetic variation would be worse than leaving it, and I agree on the evidence: the two tracks are two eligibility pathways over ONE published Coalition for Court Access bundle, and the publisher designed it that way -- the proposed order recites relief 'for an arrest, criminal charge, or juvenile delinquency allegation that did not result in a conviction', which covers both tracks in one sentence. Nothing in either track's registry entry names a field either document has and the other does not. The honest statement is therefore: THE TWO TRACKS GENUINELY PRODUCE THE SAME FILING AND DIFFER ONLY IN GUIDANCE, and after this repair they differ in guidance MORE than before, because the waiting-period paragraph is now generated from each track's own record instead of both carrying the section-1 rule.
clonedFamilyPackets.theOwnerQuestionIRaiseRatherThanAnswer: Should two packet families exist at all where one published bundle serves both tracks? CLONED_FAMILY_PACKETS.json names both families and every digest in it is stale; I did not edit it, as it is a central artifact.
clonedFamilyPackets.whatWouldMakeThemDifferAndWhyIDidNotDoIt: The only difference I could manufacture is to make both builders adopt the SAME clipping remedy, which would make the canonical packets byte-IDENTICAL rather than differing by one byte -- the opposite of what this obligation asks for, and still the right thing on the bytes.
